metadata.operator_split: Splits drawn: Cincinnati Northern Railway -> Toledo, Cincinnati & St. Louis (May 1883 consolidation); TC&StL (receivers) -> CL&N (1 Aug 1885); CL&N -> DL&C on Lebanon - Dodds (Jun/Dec 1892 lease); Middletown & Cincinnati -> CL&N (3 Jun 1902 purchase); DL&C -> CL&N north of Lebanon (Dec 1914 operation, 1 Jul 1915 ownership); CL&N -> Pennsylvania Railroad (1 Jan 1921 lease); CJ&M -> Cincinnati Northern Railroad (Jul 1897 foreclosure purchase). NOT splits: Pennsylvania Co. stock control (Mar/May 1896 - the CL&N kept operating its own property); the 1926 merger into the non-operating Pennsylvania, Ohio & Detroit; the Big Four's 1901 purchase of the Cincinnati Northern Railroad (its CL&N trains ended that year).
metadata.name_collision: Two different companies share the name: the Cincinnati Northern RAILWAY (1880-1883, the TD&B subsidiary that built and first ran this line, company string "Cincinnati Northern Railway") and the Cincinnati Northern RAILROAD (1894-1938, the CJ&M's successor, company string "Cincinnati Northern Railroad"). They keep distinct strings and colours; the labels keep the Railway/Railroad suffix so the two are not merged by name.
metadata.colour_choice: Pennsylvania Railroad reuses the existing "Pennsylvania Railroad" colour, pulled programmatically from data/. The other seven companies had no feature anywhere in data/ under any spelling (checked with a normalised search for Cincinnati Northern, Toledo Cincinnati St Louis, Lebanon and Northern, Dayton Lebanon, Middletown and Cincinnati, Jackson and Mackinaw), so each got a new hex that no other company uses.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn (Rule 1). Excluded: main line Lebanon - Cincinnati after Jan 1934 (freight to the 1980s, I&O today); Lebanon - Lytle after 1928 (ICC abandonment 1951, torn up 1952); Lytle - Hempstead - Dayton after 1928 (lifted 1979 and later); the Middletown Branch after 1917 (Hageman - Middletown still I&O freight); the Montgomery branch 1926-1933; the Court Street freight depot to 1969; the 1915 Hempstead - Clement connection (report block [12], no passenger evidence); the Penn Central / Conrail secondary tracks. The Lebanon - Hageman - Mason tourist trains (1985/88 onward) are a separate queue entry (Lebanon, Mason and Monroe Railroad) and are deliberately NOT drawn here.
metadata.horsecar_audit: Nothing to trim (Rule 5): steam from the first train. The 1875 Norwood - Walnut Hills steam dummy was proposed only; the Oak Street horse-car connection of 1881 was another company's and is not drawn.
metadata.omitted: Report blocks deliberately not drawn: [12] Hempstead - Clement (drawable NONE); [13] Dodds - Waynesville Miami Valley grade (drawable NONE, never had track); [14] tourist trains (separate queue entry); the DL&C Lambeth (1902) and NCR (1909) partial stages of the Dayton extension (drawable NONE); summer-1914 through trains (operator unknown); Dodds - Lebanon Junction passenger service 1882-1884 and DL&C service 1891-1892 (no confirmed year); the CJ&M feeder via the Big Four and the M&C north of Hageman (outside block [11]'s drawable span).
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] DL&C Lebanon - Lebanon Junction drawn 1893-1902: 1902 (a 1902 guide listing) is the last CONFIRMED year; the real end lies between 1902 and 1914, possibly c.1910 per Wikipedia's unsourced lead.
[OPEN] CL&N Lebanon - Dodds drawn 1885-1892: 1892 is the DL&C lease year; whether the CL&N kept running its own trains there afterwards is unknown.
[OPEN] Middletown & Cincinnati drawn from 1896: the earliest CONFIRMED passenger year (CJ&M through trains); the M&C's own trains probably began 1892 but are undated.
[ANCHOR] Montgomery Branch drawn 1925 only: passengers at the 14 Nov 1881 opening are inferred, not stated.

segments.note: The "Highland Route": Court Street - Walnut Hills tunnel - Avondale - Idlewild - Norwood - East Norwood - Pleasant Ridge - Deer Park - Blue Ash - Mason - Hageman - Lebanon. Cincinnati, Lebanon & Northern operations from 1 Aug 1885. 3 ft gauge until 16 Sep 1894 (dual gauge south of Idlewild from Aug 1889), standard gauge thereafter, though narrow-gauge commuter trains to Blue Ash ran on until standard equipment arrived after PRR control in 1896. Pennsylvania Co. bought a majority of the stock in Mar 1896 and PRR officers managed it from May 1896, but "the CL&N continued to operate its own property ... until January 1, 1921" - so 1896 is NOT a split. Heavy suburban commuter traffic: double track re-widened Court St - Norwood 1902-1904 "due to increased passenger traffic"; a CL&N commuter train was sideswiped in the Walnut Hills tunnel in 1916. Interurban competition (Interurban Railway & Terminal Co., Cincinnati - Lebanon) from 1903. Ends 1920 because the operator changes: leased to the Pennsylvania Railroad 1 Jan 1921 (Moody's / ICC annual reports; Baer's PRR chronology shows 1922, the ICC approval year - conflict recorded, split drawn at 1921). headway_min 60 is an ESTIMATE for the commuter peak; no frequency was found for any year.
